title: Area and perimeter of an L-shape
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can split the L into two rectangles and add their areas.
The class can find the perimeter by walking every side, including the inner steps.

modelAnswers.question: Part B of the L is 120 by 140. Find its area and then the total area of the L, given part A has area 24 000.
The six edges of an L are 200, 120, 80, 140, 120 and 260. Find the perimeter, showing the working.

commonErrors.misconception: The area of the L-shape is the length times the width of its bounding box.
commonErrors.example: A learner answers 52 000 for the area of the L on the worksheet, multiplying the 200 by 260 bounding box.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: split the L into its two filled rectangles, find each area, then add them.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: part A is 24 000 and part B is 16 800, so the total area is the sum of the two filled parts, 40 800.

commonErrors.misconception: The area of the L-shape is the length times the width of its bounding box.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner defends 52 000 by saying the L fits in a 200 by 260 box, so its area must be 200 x 260.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: point at the empty corner of the box and say whether it is part of the L, then recount only what is filled.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: the box counts an empty corner that is not part of the L, so the real area counts only the filled parts and is 40 800, never 52 000.

nextSteps: Reteach splitting composite shapes into filled rectangles before any further area questions.
Practise walking every side of a composite shape, naming the inner steps aloud, before perimeter questions.
